commands.review_summary:
The PR adds delivery-mirror marker fallback filtering, adjacent assistant duplicate collapse in replay normalization, native `tool_use` detection, regression tests, and a local repro script.

PR surface: Source +69, Tests +176, Other +283. Total +528 across 5 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main filters delivery mirrors only by provider/model and then replays surviving assistant rows without adjacent duplicate collapse. I did not run a live Telegram or provider trace in this read-only review.

target.title: fix(sessions): prevent delivery-mirror prompt contamination with adjacent dedup and identity fallback (#99470)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a delivery-mirror assistant entry gets stripped of its `provider`/`model` metadata during session rebuild or side-branch merge, it survives the transcript-only filter and leaks into the model prompt as a duplicate assistant message. In the worst case, the entry loses **all** markers (`provider`, `model`, and `openclawDeliveryMirror`), leaving only `{ role, content, usage }` — invisible to any metadata-based filter.

**Production impact**: 33% of submitted prompts were contaminated (108 of 323 `prompt.submitted` trajectory events, 278 duplicate pairs). Downstream, models conditioned on "the assistant says everything twice" mimic the pattern and emit their answer twice inside a single completion in ~2–5% of long replies — user-visible duplicated content on chat surfaces.

Fixes #99470.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three types of delivery-mirror survivors can appear in the provider-bound prompt after session rebuild, each requiring a different defence:

| Survivor type | Markers present | Caught by |
|---------------|-----------------|-----------|
| Live mirror | `provider: "openclaw"`, `model: "delivery-mirror"` | Existing main filter (Layer 0) |
| Stripped mirror | `openclawDeliveryMirror: {…}` only | **Layer 1** — identity fallback (new) |
| Bare mirror | `{ role, content, usage }` only — **no markers** | **Layer 2** — adjacent content dedup (new) |

**Layer 1 — Identity fallback**: `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` on main only checks `role`, `provider`, and `model`. When session rebuild/side-branch merge strips `provider`/`model` from a delivery-mirror entry, the entry becomes invisible to this predicate and survives into replay. Adding an `openclawDeliveryMirror` field check catches these stripped-metadata survivors.

**Layer 2 — Adjacent dedup**: When session rebuild strips **all** markers including `openclawDeliveryMirror`, the bare `{ role, content, usage }` entry is indistinguishable from a real reply to any metadata filter. `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` now collapses adjacent byte-identical assistant messages when neither carries tool calls — this is the only layer that can catch the fully-stripped bare duplicate.

**P1 fix — Native tool_use detection**: In `extractToolCallsFromAssistant()` (`tool-call-id.ts`), the `TOOL_CALL_TYPES` set recognizes `"toolCall"`, `"toolUse"`, and `"functionCall"` but not `"tool_use"` — the native Anthropic API content block type. When `isAdjacentAssistantDuplicate()` calls this helper to guard against collapsing tool-call-bearing turns, native `tool_use` blocks are invisible to the guard. Added `"tool_use"` to `TOOL_CALL_TYPES`.

**Not modified**: Session persistence logic, gateway message broadcast, user-visible transcript display.

## User Impact

Users running agents with delivery-mirror channels no longer experience prompt contamination where duplicate assistant messages inflate token usage and degrade model output quality. All three mirror types (live, stripped-marker, fully-bare) are filtered before the provider sees the prompt. Tool-call-bearing assistant turns are preserved regardless of whether the tool call uses camelCase (`toolUse`) or snake_case (`tool_use`) content blocks.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Delivery-mirror assistant entries of all three types (live, stripped-marker, fully-bare) leak into model prompt after session rebuild

**Real environment tested**: `node --import tsx`, local Node.js runtime, no external credentials required

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-99470-proof.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:

Proof script exercises the full `buildSessionContext() → normalizeAssistantReplayContent → provider-bound prompt` path against all 3 mirror types:
```
Case 0 — Session rebuild contamination path (all 3 mirror types)
  Before normalizeAssistantReplayContent (12 messages — 6 are mirrors):
    [4] LIVE-MIRROR    ← Layer 0 (existing main)
    [5] STRIPPED-MIRROR ← Layer 1 (identity fallback)
    [6] BARE-DUP       ← Layer 2 ONLY — no markers at all
    [9] LIVE-MIRROR
    [10] STRIPPED-MIRROR
    [11] BARE-DUP       ← Layer 2 ONLY

  After → 6 clean messages:
    ✓ 12→6 messages (6 delivery-mirror entries removed)
    ✓ No mirror entries in provider-bound output
    ✓ Tool-use turn preserved

Case 2 — Adjacent bare duplicate collapse (Layer 2 only, no marker)
  Uses bareDuplicate(): NO provider, model, or openclawDeliveryMirror
  Layer 1 CANNOT see this entry → only Layer 2 can collapse it
    ✓ 4→3 messages (bare duplicate collapsed)
    ✓ Real assistant reply preserved

Case 4 — Native tool_use blocks prevent collapse
    ✓ 3→3 messages (tool_use turn preserved)
    ✓ Native tool_use block present

✓ ALL PROOF CASES PASSED — provider-bound prompt is clean
```

**Observed result after fix**: All three mirror types are correctly filtered: live mirrors removed by the existing provider/model filter, stripped-marker mirrors removed by Layer 1 (identity fallback), and — critically — bare marker-free mirrors removed by Layer 2 (adjacent content dedup). Case 2 independently proves Layer 2 on entries with no `openclawDeliveryMirror` marker, addressing the P1 proof gap identified in the previous review.

Issue reporter's production verification — pre-patch: 107 of 322 `prompt.submitted` trajectory events contaminated (33%, 278 adjacent duplicate pairs); post-patch: 0 contaminants.

**What was not tested**: External provider API integration with a live model, gateway message broadcast through delivery-mirror channels, session persistence to disk, side-branch merge on a live running gateway.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  37 passed (37)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/tool-call-id.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  96 passed (96)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/tool-call-id.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts \
    src/shared/transcript-only-openclaw-assistant.ts \
    scripts/repro/issue-99470-proof.mts
→ exit 0
```
